decisions.reason: As a prominently promoted new-generation printer at the core of the firm's marking business, it likely showed enough promise to justify its higher carrying cost and supports the firm's strong growth and technology position.
This software module is closely tied to the installed base and traceability trend, and its relatively low carrying cost makes it worthwhile to retain while demand potential continues to develop.

An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces fits the firm's core application range well, so in a growing market it remains a valuable option despite the support and production effort hardware requires.

The decoding app is more peripheral than the firm's hardware systems, but as a low-cost digital complement and successor to an earlier app it is still worth keeping unless adoption clearly disappoints.

Inline code verification matches the firm's strategic move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, so the option value of staying in this area likely exceeds the cost of keeping it on the market.

Print layout design software complements the firm's coding systems directly, was given high visibility at launch, and is inexpensive to maintain relative to the strategic value of a fuller solution stack.
